claims: The Ivy League consists of eight private research universities in the Northeastern U.S.
The Ivy League consists of Harvard University, Yale University, Princeton University, Columbia University, Brown University, Dartmouth College, the University of Pennsylvania, and Cornell University.
The Ivy League was originally an athletic conference formed in 1954.
Brown University is located in Providence, RI.
Columbia University is located in New York, NY.
Cornell University is located in Ithaca, NY.
Dartmouth College is located in Hanover, NH.
Harvard University is located in Cambridge, MA.
Princeton University is located in Princeton, NJ.
University of Pennsylvania is located in Philadelphia, PA.
Yale University is located in New Haven, CT.
All Ivy League schools are located in the Northeastern United States.
All Ivy League schools are located in New York, Massachusetts, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, or New Hampshire.
As of 2025, many Ivy League schools have admission rates under 6%.
Seven of the eight Ivy League schools were founded during the Colonial era.
Cornell University was founded shortly after the Civil War.
Sticker prices (tuition and fees) for Ivy League schools are roughly around $80,000 to $95,000+ annually.
Stanford University is not in the Ivy League.
MIT is not in the Ivy League.
Duke University is not in the Ivy League.
The term "Ivy League" is based on athletic conference membership (NCAA Division I) and historical tradition.
